title: ci: set predicate-quantifier on the path filter
body:
I had a look at #2946 since the numbers turned out worse than the one example log line suggests.

The `code` filter matches **every tracked file**, not just a stray `ci.yml`. Each entry in a filter list is matched on its own and the results are OR-ed, so `'!**/*_test.go'` on its own matches everything it does not exclude. Running the filter over all 3509 files tracked on main:

```
code, default 'some'          : 3509 / 3509 files match
code, 'some-with-excludes'    : 2795 / 3509 files match

README.md                    some=true   some-with-excludes=false
.github/workflows/ci.yml     some=true   some-with-excludes=false
cmd/skopeo/copy.go           some=true   some-with-excludes=true
cmd/skopeo/copy_test.go      some=true   some-with-excludes=false
systemtest/010-inspect.bats  some=true   some-with-excludes=false
```

So the `cross`, `osx` and `ostree_rs_ext` gates on `code` never skip anything, which is the opposite of what `filters.yaml` says in its own comment.

`some-with-excludes` leaves 2795 files, all `.go`, with no `_test.go`, `systemtest/` or `integration/` among them. I checked the other two filters do not move: `all` matches 3375 either way and `docs` 171 either way, so setting this at the action level is safe.

@Luap99 the extglob trick from podman does not stretch to three excludes here, which is why I went with the quantifier instead. It is in v4.0.3, already pinned on line 34.
